comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## The leading indicator this story asks for ALREADY EXISTS — and it started working today

This story's last AC reads:

    Consider a leading indicator so the NEXT instance is not discovered by a blocked
    contributor -- e.g. a warn-level report of files above a headroom threshold, distinct from
    the existing hard-cap failure. The hard cap tells you after it is too late; nothing
    currently tells you before.

**Something does tell you before. It has been computed all along and was reporting a false zero.**

`module_size_distribution` carries a `near_cap_count` field, driven by `code_health.size_cap`
and `size_near_fraction` (default 0.1, i.e. within 10% of the cap). On merged main just now:

    module_size_distribution: {count: 435, near_cap_count: 37, over_cap_count: 0, max_loc: 799}
    oversized_module_count:   0

**37 files are within 10% of the hard cap.** That is the headroom report, live, today.

## Why nobody saw it

Two independent faults stacked, both fixed on 2026-08-05:
1. scc / lizard / jscpd were never installed, so every structural metric read `unavailable`.
2. Once scc was installed, bug c5b3-1b8a-08dd-40af meant the adapter omitted `--by-file` and
   returned a CONFIDENT ZERO -- `{count: 0, near_cap_count: 0, max_loc: 0}` -- on a repo whose
   largest file was 7011 lines.

So the indicator existed, was wired, and reported `near_cap_count: 0` for its entire life. Anyone
who looked would have concluded there was no headroom problem. That is worse than absence.

This is the same failure this session found repeatedly: the checking machinery reporting a
reassuring number it could not have computed. Cross-referenced on epic 6117-fcb7-d680-4b2f.

## What this changes for THIS story

The AC as written ("consider a leading indicator") is largely satisfied by what now works. The
remaining question is narrower and cheaper: the number is computed but nothing SURFACES it. It
appears only if someone runs `rebar metrics` and reads the field. So the residual work is:

- Decide a threshold at which 37-near-cap becomes a warning someone actually sees (CI warn step,
  or the periodic health run proposed in task 03ef-6fb5-158b-4abd, which would be a natural host).
- Do NOT build a second indicator. Wire up the one that exists.

The sweep half of this story is unaffected -- 40 files over 700 LOC, and the near-cap population
is now measurable at 37 rather than estimated.

## Caveat

`near_cap_count` depends on `code_health.size_cap` being set. It is set in `rebar.toml` (800) as
part of c5b3's dogfooding. A client that does not set `size_cap` gets `near_cap_count: null` --
so this indicator is only live for projects that configure the cap, which is worth stating
wherever it gets surfaced.

## HANDOFF — reviewed plan is PASSed and signed; implementation NOT started

Session wrapped on an operator wrap-up directive (weekly usage near limit) after the plan
passed review and the ticket was claimed, but **before any code was written**. Zero source
files were modified; no Gerrit change was pushed from this session. Returning the ticket to
`open` so a successor can pick it up. The description IS the reviewed plan — it passed
`review-plan` on 2026-08-13 (verdict PASS, attested) and needs no rewrite; a successor should
re-run `rebar review-plan <id> --status` to confirm currency against the then-current base ref
rather than re-planning.

## Re-measured survey (origin/main @ `2af5a4c773`)

435 `src/rebar` `*.py` files; **46 over 700 LOC**, 22 over 750, 7 at 796-800. The story's
original three-at-799 list is stale — all three have landed or shrunk:
`_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock.py` 799 -> 730, `_commands/init.py` 799 -> 758,
`_config_schema.py` -> 677, `_commands/fsck.py` 800 -> 301 (defaceable-icy-antelope).

Current worst, with in-flight ownership marked:

| LOC | file | status |
|---|---|---|
| 800 | `llm/plan_review/pass1.py` | **Change 1 target** |
| 800 | `_lib_writes.py` | in flight, Gerrit 1737 — HANDS OFF |
| 799 | `llm/workflow/completion_banking.py` | unowned; clean seam mapped below |
| 799 | `_store/push.py` | **Change 2 target** |
| 798 | `signing.py` | deferred -> `stealthy-appetizing-coelacanth` |
| 798 | `_engine/rebar_reconciler/binding_store.py` | unowned |
| 797 | `_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py` | unowned |
| 796 | `llm/runner.py` | unowned |
| 793 | `attest/authorship.py` | record exists (manatee) |

Also in flight and to be rebased over, not conflicting with either target: 1735 (repo-wide
typing ratchet, `effete-barbaric-xiaosaurus`), 1730, 1736, 1738, 1742.

## Extraction already staged (not committed)

Change 1's mechanical extraction was fully worked out before the stop. `container_stage.py`
comes out at **297 lines** — inside the 200-500 band, above the 100 floor — comprising
`CONTAINER_CRITERIA`, `_CONTAINER_MAX_WORKERS`, `_too_big_finding`, `build_sibling_roster`,
`_timed_pairing`, `_run_container`, with this import set (verified sufficient by inspection of
every name the moved bodies reference): `logging`, `time`, `ThreadPoolExecutor`, `Any`,
`evaluate_plan_clarity`, `capabilities`, `LLMConfig`, `LLMUnavailableError`, `Runner`,
`det_floor`, `passes`, `sizing`, `PlanContext`, and `_submit_ctx` from `.generation`.
`pass1.py` lands at ~510.

## The two traps a successor must NOT rediscover

**1. `push._git` (Change 2, load-bearing).** `push._git` is monkeypatched at ~25 sites across
10 test modules (`test_push_strict.py`, `test_epoch_guard_matrix.py`,
`test_commit_and_push_tickets_branch_heldout.py`, `test_sync_remote_config.py`,
`tests/integration/test_epoch_guard_reconciliation.py`, others), and 8 of the 9 functions
Change 2 moves call it. A module-level `from .push import _git` in the extracted module both
cycles AND binds pre-patch — the tests would keep asserting on a fake while the code ran REAL
git against the tracker. The remedy is the project's own precedent,
`_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock_push.py`: pass the calling module in as a `core` parameter
and resolve `core._git` / `core.logger` at call time. Read its §"The `core` parameter"
docstring first — it states the same rationale for the same reason.

**2. `_submit_ctx`'s placement rationale (Change 1).** It moves to `generation.py`, and the
reason matters: the pool worker it launches calls `generation.review_cancelled()`, whose
`_CANCEL_SCOPE` ContextVar is defined at `generation.py:120` — that is the generation-owned
state `copy_context()` must capture. The gate-session vars it also carries
(`_in_gate_session` / `_active_code_root`) live in `llm/gate_context.py`, NOT in
`generation.py`. Getting this backwards is what the review blocked on (see below).

## What review-plan blocked on, and why it is worth knowing

Two remediation rounds before PASS:

1. **P4, priority 1.0** — `Ticket description exceeds the review admission limit` (8051 chars
   > 8000). This fast-fails with no LLM and is easy to burn a cycle on: the store ACCEPTS a
   longer description silently, so the limit only bites at review time. Keep the description
   under 8000 characters.
2. **E4 + G6, both 0.76** — the reviewer caught a factually wrong justification: the plan
   claimed `_submit_ctx` "carries that module's [generation.py's] gate-session ContextVars",
   but those vars are defined in `gate_context.py`. I verified the reviewer was right before
   editing. The mechanism was never wrong, only the stated reason — the reviewer graded the
   RATIONALE, not just the outcome.
3. **F1, 0.85** — the "each change earns LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1" AC needed an
   `[operator-attested]` tag, since vote outcomes are Gerrit artifacts an agent cannot evaluate
   in-session.

One INDETERMINATE run also occurred (`plan-relation-snapshot-error` / `store-read-failure`)
purely because a compaction sweep from an unrelated worktree held the tickets-store write lock
for 26 minutes. That is transient, not a plan defect — retry.

## Scope judgment recorded, for whoever picks this up

The plan deliberately does NOT drain all 46 files. Per the epic, the object is the RECURRENCE
pattern. Change 3 — surfacing the near-cap indicator that ALREADY EXISTS
(`module_size_distribution.near_cap_count`, currently 37) as a non-blocking `::warning::` in
the CI Module-size gate — is the part that changes the recurrence, and it is the cheapest of
the three. If a successor has budget for only one change, **do Change 3 first**: the two
splits buy headroom in two files, but Change 3 is what stops the next instance being
discovered by a contributor who is already blocked. Note the gate lives in exactly ONE place,
the reusable `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` that both `gerrit-verify.yaml` and
`test.yml` call — `docs/architecture.md` describes it as living in the two callers, which is
true of the callers, not the step.

`completion_banking.py` (799) was outlined but not fully mapped; its `plan_recovery_batches` /
`successor_instructions` / `resolve_verifier_slot` cluster (lines ~94-321, ~230 LOC) looks like
a clean single-seam extraction with no monkeypatching on the module's own symbols. That is the
next-cheapest split after these two if the sweep continues.

## Test-count parity BASELINE recorded (for the successor)

The plan requires full-suite test-count parity per split against each change's parent commit.
That baseline was measured before the session stopped, on a **clean tree** at
`2af5a4c773925336d38697b1bb681a6fd70ce9cd` (the worktree HEAD = `origin/main` at the time),
with the exact CI-parity selection the plan names:

    pytest -m "not integration and not external" -n 3 --dist worksteal --timeout=300

    12834 passed, 60 skipped, 24 warnings in 1384.00s (0:23:03)   exit 0

**0 failed, 0 errors.** Note the clean run has NO `_no_repo_commits` teardown errors — the
guard trips only when a `git commit`/`--amend` lands while the suite is in flight (see
`defaceable-icy-antelope`'s note). If a successor sees `Test moved the repo HEAD (...)` errors,
that is their own commit overlapping the run, not a regression: check that zero tests FAILED.

Two caveats on reusing this number:

1. It is only a valid parity baseline while the parent commit is `2af5a4c773`. Several changes
   were in flight at measurement time (1730, 1735, 1736, 1737, 1738, 1742) and at least 1735
   (`effete-barbaric-xiaosaurus`) has since closed. **Re-measure at the actual parent commit**
   before claiming parity — the absolute count moves as those land.
2. Both splits are pure relocations, so the expected delta is exactly **0**. A non-zero delta
   means a test module stopped being collected — most likely an import that no longer resolves
   because a re-export was missed. That is the signal the parity check exists to catch, and it
   is the cheapest detector of the monkeypatch/re-export traps described in the handoff comment.

## Scope (revised 2026-08-13; operator-approved exception to the LOC-remediation freeze)

Re-measured on `origin/main` @ `2af5a4c773`: 435 `src/rebar` `*.py` files, **46 over 700 LOC**,
7 at 796-800. The two this story named at 799 (`_ref_lock.py`, `init.py`) are now 730/758;
`_config_schema.py` 677 and `fsck.py` 301 also landed. Worst now: `pass1.py` **800**,
`_lib_writes.py` **800** (in flight as Gerrit 1737 — OUT OF SCOPE), `completion_banking.py`
799, `_store/push.py` **799**, `signing.py` 798, `binding_store.py` 798,
`apply_inbound_records.py` 797, `runner.py` 796.

This story does **not** drain all 46: per epic `broke-boarish-hagfish` the object is the
RECURRENCE pattern, not the population. Three changes, one per file-cluster, as a small stack:
the two files at/one-line-from the cap not already in flight, plus the leading indicator this
story's last AC asks for. `signing.py` was mapped too and deferred to a `discovered_from`
record (see comments): its `_baked_commit_sha` patch-target/consumer pair forces a test edit.

---

## Change 1 — `llm/plan_review/pass1.py` 800 -> ~510

Four fused concerns: (a) the **container (G3/G4) pairing stage**, (b) the driver `run_pass1`,
(c) ISF/context blob builders (~95 LOC), (d) usage aggregation + material fingerprint (~110).
Only (a) is large enough to extract without breaching the 100-LOC floor; (c) and (d) stay with
their nearest collaborator.

**Extract to `llm/plan_review/container_stage.py` (~300 LOC):** `CONTAINER_CRITERIA`,
`_CONTAINER_MAX_WORKERS`, `_too_big_finding`, `build_sibling_roster`, `_timed_pairing`,
`_run_container`. Seam: `_run_container` has exactly ONE call site (`run_pass1`'s `if container
and ctx.has_children:` branch); `_timed_pairing`, `_too_big_finding` and
`_CONTAINER_MAX_WORKERS` are called from nowhere but `_run_container`. That call site is the
seam a previous author already cut and stopped at — the shape `defaceable-icy-antelope` found
in `fsck.py`.

**`_submit_ctx` moves to `generation.py`**, not to the new module: it is shared by BOTH
`_run_container` and `run_pass1`, so leaving it in `pass1.py` would force
`container_stage -> pass1` and cycle. `generation.py` is the right home because the worker
`_submit_ctx` launches calls `generation.review_cancelled()`, and the `_CANCEL_SCOPE` ContextVar
that reads is defined in `generation.py:120` — that is the generation-owned state
`copy_context()` must capture. (The gate-session vars `_submit_ctx` also carries,
`_in_gate_session` / `_active_code_root`, live in `llm/gate_context.py`, not here; they are
captured generically.) `generation.py`'s docstring already names `pass1._submit_ctx`. Direction
stays one-way: `pass1 -> container_stage -> generation`. `CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS` is re-derived
in `container_stage.py` from `capabilities.CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS` — the same single source
`pass1.py` reads, not a second literal.

Compatibility (semantic search AND string grep, both run): `orchestrator.py` imports
`CONTAINER_CRITERIA`, `_run_container`, `_ticket_graph_blob`, `material_fingerprint` from
`.pass1`; `provider_parity.py` imports `CONTAINER_CRITERIA` — both preserved by re-export. The ONLY symbol patched on the `pass1` module is `_shed_to_budget`
(`test_plan_review.py:2049`), whose consumer `run_pass1` STAYS, so the flamingo trap does not
arise; `_submit_ctx`, `_run_container` and `CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS` are patched nowhere. Two
source-text tests are satisfied by the re-export lines themselves:
`test_container_roster.py::test_roster_builder_single_sourced` and
`test_cache_floor_warning.py`. The only complexity-baseline key for this file is
`pass1.py::run_pass1` (20), which does NOT move: no new key, no re-key.

## Change 2 — `_store/push.py` 799 -> ~500

Concerns: (A) `_git`/`_GIT_TIMEOUT` 15 LOC, (B) **stash / dirty-tree recovery** 126, (C)
**non-fast-forward recovery** 166, (D) `_push_mode` 15, (E) S3 preflight 30, (F) commit path
114, (G) entry/driver/CLI 330. B and C form ONE subtree whose only edge into the rest is
`push_tickets_branch`'s single call to `_recover_non_fast_forward`; every other member
(`_stash_create`, `_restore_stash`, `_resolve_conflicted_apply`, `_recover_dirty_merge`,
`_merge_with_transport_retry`, `_merge_remote_under_lock`, `_fetch_for_recovery`) has one
caller, inside the subtree. **Extract B+C + `_PUSH_MERGE_LOCK_TIMEOUT` to
`_store/push_recovery.py` (~345 LOC).** A/D/E are far under the 100-LOC floor, staying with
`push_tickets_branch`; F is deliberately NOT cut — 114 LOC barely clears the floor and would
need a second late-binding seam for no headroom gain.

The hazard: `push._git` is monkeypatched at ~25 sites across 10 test modules and 8 of the 9
moved functions call it. A module-level `from .push import _git` in the extracted file
would both cycle and bind pre-patch, silently running REAL git while tests assert on a fake.
Remedy is the project's own established pattern, `_ref_lock_push.py`: each moved entry point
takes the calling module as its first `core` parameter and resolves `core._git` and
`core.logger` at call time. `_git`, `_GIT_TIMEOUT` and `logger` all stay in `push.py`, so
`push_state.py`'s `from rebar._store.push import _git`, the `rebar._store.push` logger-name
assertions in 6 test modules (including the store-epoch warning emitted from the MOVED
`_merge_remote_under_lock`), and `_bridge_runner.py`'s `python -m rebar._store.push` keep
working unchanged. `push_recovery.py` imports nothing from `push.py` — one-way.

`test_push_shared_stash_2fa6.py` calls `_push._recover_dirty_merge(...)` directly with
`push._git` patched; it gets a two-line delegating shim in `push.py`, not a test edit. `compat`
/ `lock` stay imported AS MODULES on both sides so their patch sites survive.
`.github/complexity-baseline.json` has zero keys for `push.py`.

## Change 3 — surface the leading indicator that already exists

Do NOT build a second indicator (per the 2026-08-05 comment): `near_cap_count` is computed and
reports 37, but only someone running `rebar metrics` ever sees it. The CI **Module-size gate**
already computes per-file LOC for every file it measures. Append to that
same step a NON-BLOCKING pass emitting one `::warning::` per `src/rebar` file within a headroom
band of the locked cap, exiting 0 regardless. Reuses the gate's own `find | wc -l` — no second
definition of the rule, no new file, no new failure mode, band derived from the locked limit. One edit: the gate lives only in the reusable `_build-and-test.yml`, which
both `gerrit-verify.yaml` and `test.yml` call. Policy note in `docs/architecture.md`.

## Verification, per change, before push

Full CI-parity suite (`-m "not integration and not external" -n 3 --dist worksteal
--timeout=300`) plus `tests/integration`, with **test-count parity** against the parent commit
per split; every `check_*.py` gate; every `gen_*.py` generator re-run with no diff; `make lint`;
`make typecheck`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `pass1.py` <= 550 LOC; `container_stage.py` in [100, 500]; `generation.py` <= 500.
- [x] `push.py` <= 550 LOC; `push_recovery.py` in [100, 500]. No file created by this story is
      under 100 LOC or over 550.
- [x] `pass1.<symbol>` / `push.<symbol>` attribute access preserved for every symbol named
      above; `orchestrator.py`, `provider_parity.py`, `push_state.py`, `_bridge_runner.py` and
